title: Babcock Marks Founders’ Day with Free Medical, Legal Outreach
content:
Latest Headlines
Babcock Marks Founders’ Day with Free Medical, Legal Outreach
Funmi Ogundare
Babcock University recently provided free medical and legal services for more than 300 residents of Ilishan-Remo, its host community, as part of activities marking its 67th Founders’ Day and 27th anniversary.
The initiative, which underscores the university’s commitment to sustainable community development and empowerment, enabled residents to access healthcare services and legal consultations at no cost.
The medical outreach, coordinated by the Babcock University Teaching Hospital (BUTH) medical team, offered beneficiaries specialist consultations, eye examinations and glasses, dental care, blood pressure and blood sugar checks, medications, health education, counselling and spiritual care.
The programme also included HIV screening, health talks and education, and minor and major surgical procedures.
One beneficiary, Mrs Oshitola Kujirat, thanked the university, saying she received malaria medication and treatment for pain in her leg without paying for the services. Other beneficiaries, including Mrs Bikarat Sokoni and Mrs Oluwayemi Sisadidi, also testified to the intervention’s impact.
In addition to the medical services, the university’s legal services department offered free legal consultations to residents on various issues, including landlord and tenancy disputes, land-related matters, divorce proceedings, child custody and maintenance, dissolution of marriages and estate property sharing.
The Director of Legal Services, Dr Joseph Agada, said many residents who sought legal assistance expressed satisfaction with the counsel provided.
He added that some of the cases presented during the outreach would be pursued on a pro bono basis beyond the programme, stressing that the initiative helped residents understand their rights and comply with the law.
“It’s a worthy programme that should be maintained and sustained because of its community impact, especially in helping people to know their rights and act within the ambit of the law,” he stated.
The university said that the combination of healthcare delivery and access to justice reflected its broader commitment to building resilient communities and creating lasting impact in Ilishan-Remo.
Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Babcock University, Prof. Afolarin Ojewole, said the celebration was also an opportunity to reaffirm the institution’s commitment to service.
“Our Founders’ Day is not only a celebration of heritage but also a reaffirmation of our mission to serve humanity,” he said.
He added that the outreach programmes emphasised the university’s commitment to ensuring that health, justice, and dignity are accessible to all, while building stronger relationships with its host community and beyond.

title: Herdsmen Attacks: Fear grips Delta farmers
content:
File photo
They chased a farmer and set his cargo tricycle ablaze — Vigilante chairman
By Ochuko Akuopha
For the people of Emu-Ebendo community in Ndokwa West Local Government Area of Delta State, farming is far more than an occupation; it is the foundation of their livelihoods and the heartbeat of the community’s economy.
What used to be routine trips to plantations and farmlands are now, according to residents, being undertaken with fear, as reports of encounters with armed men suspected to be herdsmen continue to unsettle the community.
The latest incidents heightened tension in the community, as the people expressed concern about their safety in the farmlands.
Last week, a farmer reportedly escaped an alleged attack after encountering a group of herdsmen in the bush while on his way to the farm.
Chairman of Emu-Ebendo Vigilante team, Mr. Fidelis Ikosa told NDV that the man was riding his Cargo tricycle to convey cassava from a farm when he allegedly sighted some armed herdsmen, in the bush.
“He went to the bush to convey cassava. On his way to the farm, he saw a group of herdsmen coming out of the bush and they started pursuing the two men in the Keke (Motorcycle cargo trailer). They now jumped out of the keke and started calling us on the phone”, he said.
He said before they could get to the place, the tricycle had been set ablaze
Ikosa said: “When we got there, we saw the keke burning. The place was close to an earth pond, so we fetched water from the pond to put out the fire.”
But while residents were still grappling with the incident, another alleged attack occurred on Monday 14th September, 2026 as a rubber tapper, Mr. John Ogoro was allegedly shot by assailants suspected to be herdsmen.
They ordered us to kneel
down — victim
Narrating his ordeal to NDV, Ogoro said “I went to my rubber plantation with my 12 years old son to see the level of flood in the place. On getting there, l decided to do some clearing. On our way back, we saw two people who accosted us and pointed guns at us. We were close to the main road.
“They accused me of killing their cows and l told them that l didn’t kill any cow that it was the first time l was entering the bush for almost two months.
“They ordered us to kneel down and we started begging them. They called two of their colleagues and they became four in number.
“One of them wanted to cut me with a cutlass but changed their mind and one said that they should use their gun, that if they use cutlass, l will shout and people will know that something was happening in the bush.
“As they were cracking their guns, l decided to stand up and run away. As l was running, they shot me on my face and on my hand and l ran with injury. I fell on the ground and started creeping on the ground.
“As l crept to the road, l fell on the ground and a good Samaritan saw me and carried me to Kwale. At that point, nobody was ready to help me because everybody was afraid.”
Ogoro said members of the Delta State Livestock Committee led by the Coordinator, Mr. Matthew Ujene were later alerted on the development and took him to “the police station with blood on my body.”
He disclosed that the police directed that he be immediately rushed to the hospital where he was given medical attention.”
Ogoro who has has been discharged from the hospital, said his son was later released by his assistants.
A good samaritan raised alarm — dslmc coordinator
Coordinator of the Delta State Livestock Management Committee in Delta North, Mr. Matthew Ujene told NDV: “l was in Kwale when a good Samaritan raised alarm that somebody was shouting for help in Umusam junction that he was rescued and dumped there.
“We quickly rushed there and carried him to the police station in Kwale where we were told to take him to the hospital. I appreciate the efforts of the hospital because they quickly attended to him without wasting time.”
Describing the situation as sad, Ujene listed Amorji, Ikonicha communities as other areas aside Emu-Ebendo where herder and farmer conflicts are taking place in Ndokwa West Local Government Area.
He called for full implementation of the State government’s anti-open grazing law.
Contacted Police Public Relations Officer of the State Command, Mr. Bright Edafe confirmed Ogoro’s attack.
He however said the victim was not shot but assaulted. “He was attacked; they broke his head but he wasn’t shot. He has been discharged and according to him, some people claimed that he killed their cow”, Edafe added.
On the lingering issue between the community and the herders, he said: “We are doing an internal investigation to know what is happening.”
We can’t really tell if it is a continuous thing for now.”

title: Unions demand paternity leave for Namibian fathers
content:
Workers’ unions are calling on the government to consider introducing paternity leave to allow both parents to care for newborn babies.
The call follows justice and labour relations minister Wise Immanuel’s announcement yesterday of an increase in Social Security Commission (SSC) benefits such as maternity and sick leave, disability, retirement and death fund, effective 1 October.
The minister announced that maternity benefits will increase from N$15 000 to N$20 000 as from 1 October, while sick leave benefits will rise from N$11 250 to N$15 000 for the first 12 months and from N$9 750 to N$13 000 for the final 12 months.
Death, retirement and disability benefits will each increase from N$12 000 to N$15 000.
Affirmative Repositioning parliamentarian Frederick Shitana says the minister had done well, but adds that men remain excluded from benefiting.
In response, the minister reiterated in the National Assembly yesterday that Namibia has no statutory paternity leave provision, adding that employers offering it do it at their discretion.
He said institutions may, however, introduce paternity leave through their respective employment or industrial policies.
“Institutions that may have paternity leave are doing it on their own and it is not prohibited in any way. They are allowed,” he said yesterday.
National Union of Namibian Workers (NUNW) secretary general Job Muniaro yesterday said men are equal parents and should be given an opportunity to support their partners and bond with their newborn babies during the early stages of parenthood.
He said women should not be left to bear the responsibilities and consequences of childbirth alone.
“Children grow healthier in the care of both parents. The mother cannot experience pregnancy and even after pregnancy alone. They need to recover,” he said.
However, he welcomed the increase, saying it would help parents meet the costs of caring for their babies, especially those earning less than N$20 000.
“The increment is long overdue, considering the cost of living and the cost of caring for a baby. It will cover 50 to 70% of workers earning below N$20 000,” he said.
Mineworkers Union of Namibia (MUN) secretary general George Ampweya yesterday said the union supports the implementation of paternity leave, describing it as a social issue.
He said men need to be present in the lives of their newborn babies.
“We are in support of benefits that support men,” he said.
“These social things we’re experiencing now may be a result of absent fathers. We are happy about the increase, although it is not absolute, it is a step in the right direction,” Ampweya said.
The union had previously made a submission to NUNW for the labour minister to introduce paternity leave.
“The current setup sort of excludes fathers from the critical years of their children. We want fathers to be able to bond and support their partners during that time,” Ampweya said.
SSC contributions are monthly payments shared equally between employers and employees to fund the maternity, sick leave and death fund.
Employees earning a basic salary of N$500, according to SSC acting chief executive Ben Nangombe, contribute N$4 per month, while those earning between N$501 and N$12 000 contribute 0.9% of their basic salary.
The Cabinet in 2023 approved the introduction of paternity leave to the Labour Act and directed that it be adopted in the public service.
It also directed the labour ministry and the Employment Creation and relevant role-players, through the tripartite taskforce, to review the Labour Act to broaden the scope of compassionate leave to cover paternity leave and the extension of the period of unpaid maternity leave from 12 to 14 weeks.

title: City Boy Movement mobilises Anambra support for Tinubu
content:
President Bola Tinubu
By Nwabueze Okonkwo
ONITSHA — The City Boy Movement, a support group campaigning for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, has taken its mobilisation campaign to Anambra State, urging residents to support the President’s second-term bid.
The group held a town hall meeting at the Prof. Dora Akunyili Women Development Centre, Awka, where speakers highlighted what they described as the benefits of maintaining a strong relationship between Anambra and the Federal Government.
The event came about a month after another pro-Tinubu group, Relax Tinubu is Fixing Nigeria (RTIFN), led by Chief John Bosco Onunkwo, held a grassroots mobilisation programme in the state.
Speaking on the theme, “Can Anambra Afford to Be Disconnected from the Centre?”, the Secretary to the Anambra State Government, Mrs Chiamaka Nnake, who was keynote speaker, urged residents to reconsider the state’s relationship with the Federal Government.
Nnake argued that supporting Tinubu’s re-election would help attract further development to Anambra, saying residents should recognise the importance of maintaining cooperation with the Federal Government.
She said the 2027 presidential election would provide an opportunity for Ndi Anambra to demonstrate their support for Tinubu and encourage him to continue his policies.
In his remarks, the South-East Coordinator of the City Boy Movement, Chief Obinna Iyiegbu, popularly known as Obi Cubana, also urged Anambra residents to support the President.
Iyiegbu said he believed the Tinubu administration was working for Nigerians despite what he described as limited support for the President in Anambra.
He pledged to take personal responsibility if Tinubu failed to deliver development to the state after receiving its support in 2027.
“I know that Tinubu is working for the people even now that he did not receive much support from the state, let alone when he wins in the state,” Iyiegbu said.
The Director-General of the City Boy Movement, Tosin Shoga, acknowledged that some Federal Government policies had imposed difficulties on citizens but argued that the measures were necessary for longer-term economic benefits.
Shoga cited Federal Government interventions, including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), ongoing infrastructure projects and appointments of Anambra indigenes to government positions, as reasons for continued support for Tinubu.
He urged residents to back the President’s re-election bid.
The Anambra State Women Leader of the movement, Mrs Adaora Soludo, called on women to remain supportive of Tinubu, saying the President meant well for the country.
Earlier, the state Director of the movement, Sir Nonso Ozoemena, urged residents to put emotions aside and consider supporting Tinubu for a second term.
He argued that Anambra could not afford to remain disconnected from the Federal Government, given the state’s economic importance.
The state coordinator of the movement, Enzo Uzor Nzeribe, said the group was established to promote the Renewed Hope Agenda, empower young people and engage Anambra residents in what he described as efforts toward a better Nigeria.
Nzeribe listed the NELFUND student loan scheme, digital skills programmes, social intervention initiatives and federal road projects among areas where he said the Tinubu administration had impacted Nigerians.
He also cited the Onitsha-Enugu and Port Harcourt-Enugu expressways, which he said were receiving Federal Government attention.
On security and welfare, Nzeribe referenced the Federal Government’s recently announced salary increase for members of the Armed Forces, describing it as a boost to the welfare of security personnel.
He said the movement was committed to sustainable youth empowerment through skills development and other initiatives designed to promote self-reliance.
Nzeribe also cited proposed and ongoing governance reforms, including state police, the creation of additional military formations and local government autonomy, as measures he said could strengthen governance at the grassroots.
Dignitaries at the event included the Anambra State Commissioner for Women Affairs, Lady Esther Onyekesi; Chief of Staff to the South-East Coordinator of the City Boy Movement, Ambassador Elijah Onyeagba; A-Big Nwankwo; and a delegation of the National Youth Council of Nigeria led by its chairman, Barrister Nonso Nwaebili.
Youths from the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and other groups also attended the event.
Highlights included a performance by the Unity Cultural Troupe and panel discussions on the role of Anambra in national development.

title: Inauguran en barrio popular de Ecuador una cancha de futbol renovada por el Chelsea
content:
Inauguran en barrio popular de Ecuador una cancha de futbol renovada por el Chelsea
El evento transcurrió en el Guasmo Norte, un barrio del sur de Guayaquil afectado por la violencia atribuida a las bandas criminales a las que el Gobierno nacional declaró la "guerra" desde 2024.
- Redacción AN / VMG
Guayaquil, la ciudad más poblada de Ecuador, se convirtió en la tercera urbe latinoamericana escogida por el Chelsea inglés para renovar una cancha de fútbol comunitaria situada en un barrio popular, y que fue inaugurada por el club, informó este viernes la Alcaldía.
“El talento puede surgir desde aquí y desde cualquier barrio y llegar a triunfar en las grandes ligas, como lo hizo nuestro ‘Niño Moi‘”, dijo durante la inauguración del campo la alcaldesa encargada de Guayaquil, Tatiana Coronel, en referencia al ecuatoriano Moisés Caicedo, jugador del Chelsea y de la selección.
El evento transcurrió en el Guasmo Norte, un barrio del sur de Guayaquil afectado por la violencia atribuida a las bandas criminales a las que el Gobierno nacional declaró la “guerra” desde 2024.
La transformación incluyó la renovación y pintura integral de la cancha de fútbol y de otro espacio más pequeño en el que se pueden practicar otros deportes como el voleibol, recuperar gradas, intervenir la fachada metálica y adecuar el lugar en general.
Además, en el sitio se pintó un mural con algunos jugadores de Chelsea, entre los que está Caicedo.
Con este proyecto, que forma parte de una campaña global del Chelsea denominada ‘Can’t Tame Us‘, el club inglés busca que el fútbol sea más accesible para las nuevas generaciones, por lo que también ha realizado remodelaciones similares en instalaciones deportivas en São Paulo y Río de Janeiro.
De acuerdo a la Municipalidad, el Chelsea asumirá durante un año el mantenimiento de las instalaciones.
Los cambios beneficiarán a unos 60 niños y adolescentes de entre 6 y 17 años que entrenan en escuelas de fútbol la zona, pero también a la comunidad, ya que, según la Alcaldía, se convertirá en un lugar de encuentro de pequeños y adultos.
El director de Deportes de la Alcaldía, Carlos Morán, explicó que el contacto con el club se dio hace un poco más de un mes y medio y, que le dijeron que habían escogido Guayaquil por ser una ciudad donde se realizan proyectos de deporte comunitario y porque es la Capital Americana del Deporte 2026.
“No solo han reconstruido una cancha, es traer esperanza para los niños, para que sigan soñando que pueden llegar a conseguir sus metas en el ámbito deportivo“, afirmó.

title: How Angel’s ‘soul dog’ helped her overcome trauma
content:
How Angel’s ‘soul dog’ helped her overcome trauma
Before training Bentley to be her support dog, Angel Oliver was living with a constant state of severe anxiety, and dealing with a rollercoaster of health issues.
But now Oliver, who struggles with anxiety, ADHD, autism and autoimmune issues, has found huge solace in having Bentley the golden digger by her side.
“I couldn’t do so many of the everyday things others take for granted, like not being able to stand in a packed lift or walk through a crowded building without a panic attack,” she said.
“I told a [dog] trainer that I can’t go to the supermarket because I get panic attacks, and they said: ‘You know if you have a disability you could actually train him and apply for him to be your assistant animal?’”
Oliver is telling her story at Darvella Patisserie in Bulimba. The cafe’s owner, Giorgina Venzin, explains to this masthead that the pair are regulars, with Bentley a particular fan of her puppacinos.
Like Venzin, Bentley is a social media star, with his life documented on Instagram under the accounts bentleythegoldendigger and brisbanedogfriendly.
Oliver originally got Bentley as a pet – “he was simply my puppy” – but as she experienced a traumatic event, and her health began to unravel, she came to rely on him more and more.
After a year of training with MindDog Australia, Bentley is now a certified support dog. He helps Oliver through companionship, deep pressure therapy and even glucose monitoring.
“He helps just by being there and helping me deal with my health issues,” she said.
The Brisbane Dog Friendly page existed before Oliver came to the city, with a mission of highlighting dog-friendly venues around the city.
Once she moved up from Melbourne in 2024 and took over the account, Oliver worked to turn it into an even stronger community.
“When I first moved to Brisbane I had no friends,” she said.
“With Brisbane Dog Friendly we straight away have one thing in common, the dog. You don’t have to be nervous about what to talk about because we have the dog to talk about.”
Oliver has also found the account to be a useful way to educate people about support dogs.
Under Queensland law, service dogs are only exempt from certain parts of health facilities, like procedure rooms, ambulances and places where food is prepared.
After letting staff know that Bentley is a support dog, most places are accommodating, although Oliver has run into a few instances of pushback.
“One time a doctor’s clinic said no [to Bentley accompanying Oliver for an appointment] even though he’s a service dog,” she said.
“Everyone has different rules and I respect that.”
For Oliver, Bentley is more than just a pet. “He’s my soul dog – a very companionship type of dog. He’s very bubbly, he will make you feel special.”

title: Relance du Programme spécial de désenclavement : le ministre Déthié Fall en mission à Dubaï

Relance du Programme spécial de désenclavement : le ministre Déthié Fall en mission à Dubaï
Le ministre des Infrastructures, des Transports terrestres et du Désenclavement, Déthié Fall, a conduit une importante délégation composée de représentants du ministère des Finances et de l’Ageroute pour rencontrer les dirigeants du groupe Innovo (anciennement ASGC). L'objectif de cette mission est d'acter la relance effective du Programme spécial de désenclavement (PSD).
Un programme stratégique pour l'économie et les territoires
Ce programme ambitieux porte sur la construction et la réhabilitation de 2 000 kilomètres de routes et de voiries à travers l’ensemble du territoire national. Il mobilise plus de 60 entreprises sénégalaises du BTP et devrait générer plus de 55 000 emplois directs et indirects.
À l’arrêt depuis 18 mois, le projet s’inscrit directement dans la vision du chef de l’État en faveur d’un Sénégal inclusif et d’une véritable équité territoriale. Redémarrage fixé pour février 2027 et prochaine étape à Londres]

Après cette première étape émiratie, une autre réunion stratégique est prévue dans les prochains jours à Londres avec les partenaires financiers. title: B.C. judge rules Vancouver city candidates can use Chinese names on ballot
content:
B.C. judge rules Vancouver city candidates can use Chinese names on ballot
Judge Roger Cutler released his decision on Friday, but his written reason will come later
Seven Vancouver city candidates who included Chinese characters in their “usual” name can have them on the ballot for the municipal election, after the city lost a court challenge on Friday.
Judge Roger Cutler of the B.C. provincial court said each of the seven applicants would be allowed to use their usual names on the ballot for the Oct. 17 election and that he would issue his reasons for his decision at a later date.
Cutler said his decision should not be taken as a statement that the city’s application wasn’t appropriate, and his written reasons will provide guidance for future elections.
Lawyers for the city and for the candidates submitted arguments to Cutler on Wednesday and on Friday morning, and Cutler took five minutes after lunch to announce his decision.
The “usual names” in all seven cases included Chinese characters in addition to their “English” names, and the candidates argued the Vancouver Charter allowed that.
The city took the case to court, saying it wanted guidance on whether the Chinese character names were their “usual” names and whether they should be allowed on the ballots.
Cutler presided over the hearing by video from Duncan to eliminate any perception of bias from a Vancouver-based judge.
City lawyer Grant Murray told the court he would inform the chief election officer of the decision and that the decision had come in time for the lottery draw to determine the order of names on the ballots that was scheduled to be held at 5 p.m. Friday.
“I’m relieved by the decision,” Iona Bonamis, who’s running for city council under the OneCity party banner, said by phone.
She said hopefully it will mean candidates in future will be able to include the names they are known by in their community without having to go through a court battle.
A message left with the city for comment was not returned on Friday.
The city’s chief election officer, Jason Twa, had argued the seven Chinese character names were not part of their usual names.
In addition to Bonamis, whose name is 陶思穎 (To Sie Wing), the other candidates are current ABC councillor Lenny Zhou or 周楠 (Zhou Nan) and Christopher Lee, a OneCity school board candidate, whose Chinese name is pronounced Lee Kei Peng (李基鵬).
Others using Chinese character names are Yuk (Alfred) Chien (錢育廷), Yunzia (Chris) Qiu (仇云霞), Lorraine Lowe (刘黛明) and Shirley SiO (邵己凌). Lowe is running for city council, Qiu for park board and Chien and SiO for school board.
During his submissions, Murray had told court that all the candidates, with the exception of Bonamis, appeared to exclusively use their English names and not their Chinese names on social media.
And he said that it was “odd” that the candidates hadn’t included their “usual” Chinese names on their original filings but added them later, at the last minute.
Of the 123 candidates for council, park board and school board published on the City of Vancouver’s website, seven included a Chinese name.
The Charter is the unique provincial legislation that governs the City of Vancouver. According to the Charter, nomination papers must include the full name of the person nominated and “the usual name of the person nominated, if the full name of the person is different from the name the person usually uses.”
Bonamis said earlier if the court allowed her to use her name, it would send a message that Vancouver respects different cultures and that it’s a multicultural city.
Lee, 18, said it’s important for him to have the name on the ballot because “it’s a core part of my identity.”
“I’m a very proud Canadian. I’m also a very proud Chinese Canadian,” he said. “Canada is a multicultural place and we should respect that, the electoral office should respect that.”
“I don’t think it’s about having the Chinese name on the ballot to win votes, it’s about … our identity. It’s what the people in the Chinese community know us as.”
It’s a sign that we can “represent every single voice that Vancouver has,” he said.

title: Inondations à Coyah et Manéah : les sinistrés attendus chez eux dès mercredi
content:
Conakry – La situation évolue favorablement à Coyah et Manéah après les inondations enregistrées ces derniers jours. Le niveau des eaux a considérablement baissé, permettant aux autorités d’envisager le retour des sinistrés dans leurs domiciles à partir de mercredi.
Selon Lancei Touré, directeur général de l’ANGUCH, huit personnes légèrement blessées ont été prises en charge à l’hôpital préfectoral de Coyah. L’agence a également mis en place des sites d’hébergement pour accueillir les familles évacuées.
« Il y a huit blessés légers qui ont été déposés à l’hôpital préfectoral de Coyah. Et ensuite, l’ANGUCH a ouvert immédiatement, comme d’habitude, des lieux d’hébergement pour les sinistrés. On a la Maison des Jeunes, où on a hébergé 218 personnes, et ensuite, au niveau de Bananeraie, une école », a-t-il déclaré.
Concernant les personnes toujours hébergées, le responsable de l’ANGUCH assure que leur retour est prévu dès mercredi, en raison de la décrue observée sur le terrain.
« Le cas de Manéah et de Coyah, ils vont passer la nuit là-bas pour sauver leur vie et on va les libérer mercredi. Parce que déjà, il y a eu des décrues, donc le niveau de l’eau a considérablement baissé. Et à partir de mercredi, on va les libérer », a-t-il déclaré.
Les opérations d’assistance et d’évaluation se poursuivent dans les zones touchées, alors que les autorités suivent l’évolution du niveau des eaux avant le retour définitif des familles.

title: Aunque también verás castaños, hayas o abedules, en esta ruta descubrirás uno de los mejores robledales de la cornisa cantábrica
content: El Robledal de Ucieda, parte del Parque Natural Saja-Besaya, es todo un verdadero refugio de biodiversidadEl pequeño pueblo de un patrimonio enorme: una alhóndiga, una muralla, dos puentes, un castillo, una ermita e incluso un verracoLa ruta por esta Reserva Natural te llevará a ver una ermita, una fuente que alberga una leyenda y carpes, árboles poco comunes en la península Considerado uno de los espacios forestales mejor conservados de la región, el Robledal de Ucieda se despliega majestuoso en el Parque Natural Saja-Besaya. Aunque también verás castaños, hayas o abedules, en esta ruta descubrirás uno de los mejores robledales de la cornisa cantábrica. Esta impresionante masa boscosa abarca más de 3.600 hectáreas entre las cuencas de los ríos Saja y Besaya, ofreciendo un verdadero refugio de biodiversidad. Al recorrer sus frondosos senderos, el caminante experimenta una inmersión sensorial única donde las densas copas filtran la radiación solar y pintan matices dorados sobre el suave manto de hojarasca del suelo boscoso. La riqueza vegetal de este monte atlántico destaca por la convivencia armónica de robles centenarios, conocidos como cajigas, junto a hayas, castaños, abedules, acebos, alisos y avellanos. Entre las joyas botánicas resalta el célebre Roble Tumbao, ejemplar singular que cayó hace más de un siglo, pero logró sobrevivir haciendo crecer sus ramas verticales hacia la luz solar. En otoño, la arboleda brinda un espectáculo cromático incomparable, desplegando una paleta de tonos ocres, cobrizos y rojizos que viste la ladera montañosa. La protección institucional ha permitido catalogar una decena de ejemplares veteranos como Árboles Singulares de Cantabria, garantizando así su preservación. El vínculo histórico entre la población local y el monte de Ucieda se remonta a la Edad Media, época en la que los habitantes del valle de Cabuérniga aprovechaban los recursos de forma sostenible. De los bosques se extraía madera imprescindible para edificar viviendas tradicionales, fabricar herramientas de labranza y elaborar carbón vegetal para las ferrerías autóctonas. Asimismo, floreció la destacada artesanía de la ebanistería, conocida como Garaúja, que mantenía la actividad económica familiar durante los prolongados inviernos. Como testimonio de aquel valioso patrimonio cultural, Ucieda conserva soberbias casonas montañesas de los siglos XVII y XVIII, entre las que sobresalen los palacios de Quirós y Escagedo. La protección institucional ha permitido catalogar una decena de ejemplares veteranos garantizando así su preservación Para explorar este enclave natural parten diversas rutas de senderismo desde la antigua serrería de la Casa del Monte, espacio transformado hoy en un popular punto de acogida y área recreativa. Destaca la amena Ruta de los Puentes, itinerario circular que bordea el cauce del río Bayones y permite cruzar arroyos cantarines a través de románticas pasarelas de madera. Quienes buscan mayor reto pueden emprender la Ruta de Hayacorva, ascendiendo más de 500 metros de desnivel hacia el refugio de Urizosas y las inmediaciones del alto del Toral. El trazado regala soberbias vistas panorámicas hacia las divisorias de los valles cantábricos, combinando tramos de pista cómoda con senderos tradicionales inmersos en la espesura del sotobosque. La fauna autóctona encuentra en el dosel boscoso de Ucieda un hábitat ideal para alimentarse y reproducirse lejos de las agresiones urbanas. Durante la estación otoñal, el bosque vibra con el ritual de la berrea, momento en que los majestuosos ciervos machos emiten sus potentes bramidos para atraer a las hembras. Entre el follaje también es habitual avistar cautelosos corzos y detectar rastros de jabalíes, mientras las aves encuentran un refugio privilegiado. Los observadores de avifauna pueden admirar especies como el picamaderos negro, el herrerillo capuchino, el trepador azul o el carismático mirlo acuático en las cristalinas aguas del río Bayones, custodiadas desde las alturas por el vuelo majestuoso del águila real. Tradiciones arraigadas La cultura de la comarca se halla estrechamente ligada al entorno natural a través de celebraciones tradicionales arraigadas en el sentir popular. Un ejemplo es cuando la campa de Ucieda acoge la afamada Fiesta del Cocido Montañés, un evento de Interés Turístico Regional que ensalza la gastronomía tradicional cántabra. Asimismo, las brañas del monte celebran la romería festiva de Nuestra Señora del Moral, hermanando a los valles vecinos en una cita entrañable. Muy cerca del robledal se pueden visitar otros hitos de interés patrimonial, como la mágica Fuentona de Ruente con su leyenda de la anjana, el histórico conjunto de Carmona o el asombroso bosque de secuoyas gigantes ubicado en la frondosa localidad de Cabezón de la Sal. La conservación de este valioso ecosistema caducifolio constituye un compromiso prioritario dentro de la estructura de la Reserva de Caza Saja. En las laderas de Collaverde se ubica un rodal selecto de roble dedicado a la recolección de bellotas para la mejora genética de las masas forestales de Cantabria. Este valioso trabajo silvícola asegura que las futuras generaciones continúen disfrutando de un paisaje saludable y resistente ante los retos ambientales. Visitar el Robledal de Ucieda supone recorrer un santuario viviente de historia, biodiversidad y belleza natural, donde los robles veteranos permanecen firmes como guardianes de la montaña cantábrica, invitando al caminante a contemplar la serenidad del monte.

title: Abkommen mit den USA – Die grössten Sieger könnten die Grönländer selbst sein
content:
Grönland ist nicht nur die grösste Insel der Welt, sondern auch sehr begehrt. Gerade das Begehren und Gebaren von US-Präsident Donald Trump hat in den vergangenen Monaten für geopolitische Spannungen gesorgt. Nun haben die USA, Dänemark und Grönland ein Sicherheitsabkommen unterzeichnet. Nordeuropa-Korrespondent Bruno Kaufmann erklärt, was das für die Grönländerinnen und Grönländer bedeutet.
SRF News: Wie viel hatte Grönland mitzureden bei diesem Vertrag?
Bruno Kaufmann: Sehr viel – und das ist erstaunlich, wenn man die Verhältnisse kennt. Im grönländischen Aussenministerium sind 25 Menschen angestellt. Zum Vergleich: Das Schweizer Aussendepartement hat über 5000 Mitarbeitende. Es ist also ein extrem kleines Team, das sehr gute Arbeit für Grönland geleistet hat.
Viele Grönländerinnen und Grönländer sind erschöpft. Sie konnten nicht mehr schlafen, waren verunsichert.
Unterstützung bekommen haben sie auch vom dänischen Aussenminister Lars Løkke Rasmussen, der eine gewisse Sensibilität für diese Themen entwickelt hat. Seine Frau kommt von den Färöer-Inseln.
Was bringt der Vertrag Grönland konkret?
Zunächst eine Atempause. Viele Grönländerinnen und Grönländer sind erschöpft. Sie konnten nicht mehr schlafen, waren verunsichert. Sie haben aufs Meer hinausgeschaut. Und wenn sie ein Militärschiff gesehen haben, wussten sie nie: Ist das ein Feind oder ein Freund? In den sozialen Medien wurden ständig Karten aus dem Weissen Haus aufgeschaltet, die Grönland unter amerikanischer Flagge zeigen. Diese täglichen «Übergriffe» aus Washington haben die Grönländerinnen und Grönländer sehr gestresst. Vielleicht tritt jetzt ein bisschen Ruhe und Sicherheit ein.
Vielleicht tritt jetzt ein bisschen Ruhe und Sicherheit ein.
Der Vertrag ist eine Riesenchance für Grönland, sich selbstständig als Inuit-Staat weiterzuentwickeln. Grönland ist ein Land voller Möglichkeiten, aber auch ein Land, in dem die Menschen wissen, was es braucht, um zu überleben. Und das können sie selbst am besten. Aber nicht alleine, sondern mit Unterstützung, mit Zusammenarbeit. Man hofft, dass dieser Vertrag jetzt die Grundlage dafür bietet.
Im Vertrag steht auch, dass die USA mehr Einfluss bekommen sollen, wer in Grönland in sicherheitsrelevante Infrastrukturen investieren darf. Was bringt das Grönland?
Die Schweiz ist als neutraler, wohlhabender Staat fähig, selbstständig in der Welt zu bestehen. Das ist für die Grönländerinnen und Grönländer, was die Natur betrifft, eine Selbstverständlichkeit. In der Weltpolitik geht es jedoch nicht ohne Unterstützung. Deshalb ist und war man schon lange an engeren Beziehungen zu Kanada, aber auch zu den USA interessiert, um nicht einseitig abhängig von Dänemark zu sein.
Das wird für Grönland eine Möglichkeit sein, weiterzukommen und als modernes Land in der Welt mitzubestimmen.
Entscheidend ist die völkerrechtliche Absicherung, die im Vertrag formuliert ist. Das wird für Grönland eine Möglichkeit sein, weiterzukommen und als modernes Land in der Welt mitzubestimmen.
Also ist dieser Vertrag eine Art Win-Win-Win-Situation für alle Beteiligten?
Ich denke schon. Eine stabile Lösung für den Nordatlantik kann für die USA ein Sieg sein, gerade für Präsident Trump. Auch für Dänemark, das hier als Schutzmacht für Grönland eine aussenpolitische Krise erlebte, ist es ein Riesengewinn, wenn der alte Alliierte Amerika nicht plötzlich als Feind gesehen wird, der alles infrage stellt. Aber die grössten Siegerinnen und Sieger könnten die Grönländerinnen und Grönländer selbst sein. Denn es ist ihre Gesellschaft, ihre Natur, ihr Land, das sie seit Jahrtausenden bewohnen. Wenn es gelingt, dass sie das auch weiterhin machen können, ist das natürlich ein enormer Erfolg.

title: How the NPR College Podcast Challenge changed lives
content:
How the NPR College Podcast Challenge changed lives
Catch up on what you missed with our Education newsletter, sent weekly.
I was in my final stretch of college, during the height of the pandemic. I was holed up in my house in Colorado Springs, Colo., doing homework at the dining room table, when my phone rang. NPR education reporter Sequoia Carrillo was on the line, calling to tell me I had won the 2021 College Podcast Challenge.
It sounds dramatic, but that phone call changed my life. Winning the challenge helped land me my first job in radio at KNKX, an NPR member station in Seattle. Now, I'm a freelance journalist, working on the next season of Inheriting, from LAist and NPR. I've reported stories all over — from Owens Valley, Calif., to New York City — and have met some unforgettable people along the way.
Five years later, as the annual contest returns for another round, I reached out to a few other past participants to see if their lives changed as much as mine.
Reconnecting with family
Miriam Colvin was a freshman at Penn State University in 2021 when she became one of two winners in the inaugural College Podcast Challenge. In her podcast, she dove into family lore about a fateful boxing match between her grandpa's friend and a teenage Muhammad Ali — or Cassius Clay as he was known back then.
Winning gave her the courage to pursue a career in stand-up comedy and playwriting. Over the years, Colvin has found herself returning to the elders in her life for creative inspiration. She loves hearing her grandpa talk about his childhood in Indiana, which he spent climbing bridges, catching birds and driving the family car around at 11 years old.
"These stories remind me we need to be out living, doing adventurous stuff with our loved ones, with our friends," she says.
As Colvin has grown up, her grandparents' stories have also taken on more meaning for her. Even though the world they grew up in feels unfamiliar, she's come to recognize parts of herself in these stories.
"As you get older, you kind of realize that we're all doing the same thing, and we all went through challenges and had growing pains."
For Bunmi Omisore, the struggle was not just to preserve family stories, but to understand them in the first place. Her podcast, which received an honorable mention in 2025, documented the early stages of her journey to learn her parents' native language, Yoruba.
" While it's very easy for me to be like, 'Well, my parents didn't teach me, so they can't be mad that I don't understand,' it's like, they still speak the language," she explains. "I'm the only person who loses out by deciding not to learn."
After making the podcast, Omisore, a senior at Duke University at the time, got serious about learning. Her father started speaking to her only in Yoruba over the phone. Her copy of Beginner's Yoruba became water-stained and covered in pencil marks. A year later, all that hard work has paid off.
"If you were to tell me two years ago, that I would be able to understand my parents only speaking Yoruba, I'll admit it, I would not have believed you."
For Omisore, the most rewarding part has been gaining access to a deeper understanding of her Nigerian family. There's a video of her grandmother she remembers seeing growing up, where her grandmother is speaking in Yoruba while playing with her goats. Now, she can hear that her grandmother is cracking jokes about the goats, pretending they're her pet dogs.
"She had a sense of humor, she had wit, all these things that I was not able to embrace because I didn't know the language," Omisore says. "It humanized a woman that I had known that I had come from, but I hadn't really been able to understand."
A step closer to a dream career
Bennett Cook is not just a transit enthusiast — he prefers the term transitologist. He entered the College Podcast Challenge in 2021, as a student at Buffalo State University, with a story about the unexpected music subway trains make.
Hearing that music is "very rare," Cook says. "You'd have to really turn to your sixth sense." But, he says, if you listen closely, the train's machinery might evoke the sound of cellos, or even a violin, as it departs a station.
Cook says that being named a finalist in the competition fueled his drive to pursue his passion as a career.
He got a job with the Chicago Transit Authority earlier this year, making the move hundreds of miles away from his home in New York City. Now he spends his days as a customer service assistant, helping others navigate the transit system, which he already knows by heart.
Cook hasn't stopped dreaming — he wants to become the person operating the trains, and he has big ideas about how Chicago can expand its transit system that he hopes he can put into motion someday.
The College Podcast Challenge also launched Jo Strogatz into her dream job. In 2024, she was a student at Salt Institute for Documentary Studies in Maine when she won the contest. Her story featured her own original music and an interview with a friend, who is in his 60s, and who has never had a romantic relationship before.
Strogatz works at Radiolab now, a role she believes she never would've landed without the contest.
"I can't believe that I'm so lucky to have this opportunity to be at a place where I can do science and storytelling and learn from people every day," she says.
Edited by: Janet Woojeong Lee and Nirvi Shah

title: Jenni Scharingers letzter Weg: Abschied einer Vielgeliebten
content: Unmenschliches hat die Familie Scharinger in den vergangenen acht Jahren durchgestanden. Auf der Suche nach ihrer Tochter, ihrer Schwester, die seit 22. Jänner 2018 spurlos verschwunden war. Und deren Ex-Partner im vergangenen August zu lebenslanger Haft plus Unterbringung in einem forensisch-therapeutischen Zentrum verurteilt wurde; nicht rechtskräftig.Doch diese Tage sind die Schlimmsten. Am kommenden Wochenende wird das Begräbnis von Jenni Scharinger in Hanfthal, Bezirk Mistelbach, stattfinden. In der Pfarrkirche jenes kleinen Ortes, in dem Jenni aufgewachsen ist. „Vor dem Begräbnis habe ich Angst“, sagt Mutter Brigitta. Denn dann ist der Abschied von ihrer jüngsten Tochter endgültig. Jeden Tag, so beschreibt es die Mutter, gönne sie es sich, „ein paar Mal zu plärren“.All die Jahre zuvor hatte sie ihre gesamte Energie in die Suche nach Jenni gesteckt. Indizien gegen den Ex-Freund gab es viele. Doch Beweise oder ein Geständnis fehlten. Also fing die Mutter mit Unterstützern selbst an, zu ermitteln. Die Suche nach der Leiche ihres Kindes führte sie auch in die Wälder, in denen sie mit dem Spaten unzählige Gruben aushob, um endlich Jennis sterbliche Überreste zu finden. Zuletzt war es eine List, die Jennis Mörder überführte. Ein anonymes Gespräch über eine Dating-Plattform, in dem der Mann darüber sprach, wie er eine Leiche am besten verschwinden lassen würde.Später legte der 33-jährige bei der Polizei ein Geständnis ab, führte die Ermittler zu Jennis sterblichen Überresten auf dem Truppenübungsplatz Allentsteig.Den Prozess verfolgte Jennis Mutter nicht. Sie wollte mit Clemens T. nicht im selben Raum sein. Jennis Schwester vertrat die Familie, viele Freundinnen der damals 21-Jährigen waren anwesend. „Jetzt kann er niemandem mehr etwas antun“, sagt die Mutter.Schon in der Vorwoche nahm sie am „Gehen gegen Gewalt“ teil. „Weil das aufhören muss. Es darf nicht so weitergehen!“Es soll ein würdiger Abschied von ihrer Tochter werden, wünscht sie sich. Auch die Sängerin Oska wird ihren Teil dazu beitragen. Die Amadeus-Preisträgerin wird unter anderem „You are my Sunshine“ singen. „Weil Jenni unser Sonnenschein war.“

title: Philippine poverty rate falls below 10%, India delivers eight million HPV vaccines, adapted sailing
content:
Photo: Sian Labay/Unsplash (CC0)
In today’s edition: The Philippines brings its poverty rate below 10%, India reaches eight million HPV vaccinations, and adapted sailing is opening up the freedom of the sea to people with reduced mobility.
Around 6.5 million Filipinos moved above the poverty line between 2023 and 2025. With poverty incidence now at 9.7%, the focus shifts to keeping families from slipping back: sustained jobs, incomes, and targeted support will be key to making these gains last.
Source: Rappler
Indonesia is paying villagers to photograph wildlife instead of hunt it, creating a practical alternative to hunting whilst generating valuable data on threatened species. The cash-for-photos programme has already produced more than 350,000 wildlife observations, and two participating villages have voluntarily banned hunting.
Source: Aawsat
India has delivered more than eight million HPV vaccinations as part of a nationwide effort to prevent cervical cancer before it starts. The campaign offers 14-year-old girls a voluntary, free, single-dose vaccine against HPV, the infection responsible for most cervical cancer cases.
Source: New Indian Express
As Russian attacks target Ukraine’s electricity grid, solar power is helping homes, businesses and communities keep essential services running. The country added 1.5 GW of solar capacity in 2025, nearly twice the previous year, while rooftop panels and batteries provide a lifeline during outages.
Source: Grist
Seattle Public Schools will begin offering free meals to all students, removing cost as a barrier to school meals. The programme is funded by about $4.7 million from a voter-approved education levy for the 2027-28 school year, with a new state tax on high earners expected to fund the programme after this.
Source: Seattle Times
From bedtime stories to book clubs, reading for pleasure could do more than entertain: new data link it to better attention and memory, alongside fewer mental health problems. Researchers at the University of Cambridge say the findings add to evidence that reading can support cognitive health from childhood into old age, and that it’s never too late to start.
Source: Euronews
The familiar call to “save the bees” can obscure a crucial distinction: managed honeybees and threatened wild pollinators face very different ecological challenges, according to entrepreneur Noah Wilson-Rich. A closer look at bee conservation offers a clearer path to action, from protecting native habitats to supporting the wild pollinators ecosystems depend on.
Source: NHPR
Pesticide use in Kenya has risen steadily over the past few decades: pesticide imports surged from 6,400 tonnes in 2015 to more than 15,600 tonnes in 2019, with farmers now spending an estimated $70m (£52m) annually. However, a growing number are recognising both the health and environments these products bring with them and are turning to more sustainable alternatives.
Source: The Guardian
Female glowworms were spotted over multiple weeks at Nosterfield nature reserve this summer following a no-frills, almost zero-budget reintroduction of the much-loved invertebrates, which have vanished from the British countryside in recent decades and are notoriously difficult to re-establish.
Source: The Guardian
Accessible boats and specialised sailing schools are helping people with reduced mobility experience the freedom of the open water. At Spain’s Monte Real Yacht Club, free adapted sailing lessons and custom-built boats have been opening up the sport to people with functional diversity since 2012. Similar programmes around the world are using inclusive design to make new spaces accessible to all.
Source: Reasons To Be Cheerful

title: The site of India’s maiden gold: Between a bench and baseball cage
content:
Stay updated with the latest sports news across Cricket, Football, Chess, and more. Catch all the action with real-time live cricket score updates and in-depth coverage of ongoing matches.
There is a toilet, a bench and a baseball cage, the only permanent structures. And then there is the cricket pitch — the latest addition.
Korogi Athletic Park is almost too open, too green, too tranquil to be an international sporting venue. Even Harmanpreet Kaur, the India captain, knew this was a nation hardly associated with cricket. “But knowing Japan, we knew they would manage something,” she said.
They had managed something that looked quite a lot like a quaint English county ground.
On Tuesday afternoon, in this unlikely setting in the middle of a public park in Nisshin, on the outskirts of Nagoya, India won the first gold medal of its Asian Games campaign. They beat Sri Lanka by 147 runs, so comprehensively that the suspense had disappeared long before the celebrations.
When the celebrations finally came, Radha Yadav and Renuka Thakur started sprinting towards the middle with the Indian flag. Then they slowed to a walk, almost as if they had realised there was no need to hurry. The final had been so one-sided that even the celebration seemed to have time to spare.
But the people watching did not seem to mind.
Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage
A Sri Lankan family had driven for a couple of hours from Nara to be here. There were Indians from England, on holiday in Seoul, who had made their way to Nisshin to watch India play.
And then there were the Japanese. For many of them, this was their first cricket match. “I have come to watch because my daughter has married a Sri Lankan man,” said one spectator. An elderly couple, Naofumi and Chisato, had seen children practice baseball hits here, and came for cricket just out of curiosity. “We know nothing about it,” Naofumi said.
They had been handed a beginner’s guide in Japanese explaining the rules and were repeatedly looking down at them, then back at the field, trying to make sense of what had just happened. A wicket, a boundary, a change of bowler — moments that require no explanation to a cricket audience were being learnt in real time.
Mimi Hirayama, the public announcer, was helping them along. “Mainly rules, because the Japanese audience is not familiar with this sport,” Hirayama said. “But they are very familiar with baseball. So I’ll keep giving them my hints to understand what’s going on.” So a six became a home run. “And when the batter hits four, it’s like a three-base hit or something like that,” Hirayama said.
It was an ingenious way of introducing cricket to an audience that already understood another bat-and-ball sport.
Hirayama could make the comparisons because she had spent many years in England and was familiar with cricket. Before the Games, she also watched matches involving India and other countries to learn more about the sport.
For a few hours, then, Korogi contained several different versions of cricket fandom at once: Indians celebrating, Sri Lankans supporting their team, an overseas diaspora making an unexpected detour, and Japanese spectators discovering the game through baseball.
It was an unusual scene for a ground that, until recently, was not a cricket ground at all.
Korogi is a public ground that has facilities for baseball, tennis and football, which is where the teams trained, too. When cricket was added to the Asian Games programme at the last minute, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha said she helped finalise this geound as the venue. And so, the baseball ground was converted for the Games between September last year and March 2026. The 305 million yen (approximately Rs 18 crore) project involved relaying 14,984 square metres of grass, installing practice nets and building an equipment store. It hosted six matches of the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup East Asia-Pacific Qualifier in May as its first major test.
Now it has hosted an Asian Games final — and India’s first gold of these Games.
Harmanpreet said the only adjustment the team had to make was playing on the hybrid pitches. “But we knew how the pitch would behave because recently in England, we played on hybrid pitches too. The other facilities weren’t of top level but they managed it pretty well, she added.
Once the flags come down, Nisshin mayor Hiroki Kondo said the cricket will continue. “This is the second ground in Japan after Sano. After the Asian Games we will continue playing cricket here along with baseball,” Kondo said.
How often?
“About 18 days.”
A month?
“No. This is Japan — 18 days a year.”
It might not be much, but Hirayama hopes it will be just enough to keep the link with the sport alive. “I hope many people here in Japan, who have found this sport exciting and think they will enjoy it enough to play,” Hirayama said. “So I hope this ground will also be used for cricket in the future.”
Soon, Jasprit Bumrah and India’s men will walk out onto the same strip. And, somewhere between the baseball cage and the toilet, cricket has found a place to stay.

title: From Mountain Range to Economic Bridge: Bukovel’s C8 Opens New Chapter for Europe
content:
The inaugural Carpathian Eight (C8) Summit in Bukovel ended yesterday with an air of positivity and goodwill towards transforming the Carpathian region into a confluence of security, economic development, and investment.
For centuries, the Carpathian Mountains have been a geographical feature dividing and connecting Central and Eastern Europe. This week, they became something more: a formative binding of eight nations around a common economic, security and cultural future.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Hosted by President Volodymyr Zelensky, the C8 Summit, held from Sept. 18-19 in picturesque Bukovel in the Ivanko-Frankivsk region, brought together Austria, Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia and Ukraine, alongside EU institutions, business leaders and international investors in support of Ukraine.
The significance goes well beyond another regional summit.
The Carpathians are emerging as a bridge between Ukraine and the EU – geographically, economically, culturally and increasingly in terms of security. The optimism was palpable with keynote speakers openly using the word “when,” and not “if,” Ukraine joins the EU.
President Zelensky described the initiative as, “a new framework for cooperation encompassing security, energy, logistics, cross-border economic development and support for communities.”
The region covers some 200,000 square kilometers and is home to 20 million people, creating an opportunity to move beyond viewing the Carpathians as a collection of national markets and, instead, combining them as a single, interconnected, economic and security region.
Denmark Expedites $275M Military Aid Package for Ukraine
From mountains to markets
The economic opportunity was a central theme of the C8 Summit.
On the table are some 90 investment and trade projects with an estimated value of nearly $11 billion covering energy, infrastructure, oil and gas, transport and logistics, manufacturing, agritech, healthcare, and culture.
Hydro and renewable energy held the spotlight, leveraging the natural resources of the Carpathian’s rivers. Ukraine has ingeniously promoted the concept of the mountain region becoming an energy supplier to the EU rather than simply a transit corridor.
Agriculture and agritech were highlighted as another significant opportunity, linking the agrarian capabilities of Ukraine and its neighbors with processing, logistics and access to the EU single market. The summit program specifically identified the development of value chains from local producers through to processing and distribution among European markets.
Construction, infrastructure and real estate were also central to the emerging regional investment story, particularly as Ukraine’s reconstruction increasingly intersects with the economies and supply chains of neighboring European states.
And beyond individual sectors, the broader opportunity for private capital, joint ventures and public-private partnerships, together with cross-border investment platforms, was a constant theme among delegates, viewing the C8 countries as an interconnected economic space rather than isolated markets.
In support of that, Prime Minister, Serhii Koretskyi has called for greater mutual investment, international capital through joint regional platforms, and C8 involvement in Ukraine’s reconstruction as a shared regional economic project.
Security as an economic Issue
The perennial issue of security was not far from lips of all speakers, including those whose prime focus was economic, highlighting the rapidly changing dynamics of the European security environment.
While C8 countries already cooperate across defense, energy, transport and humanitarian networks, the summit sought to strengthen those existing relationships into a more structured regional framework.
And that matters economically.
Secure borders, resilient energy systems, reliable transport corridors and protected infrastructure are prerequisites for capital investment. The Carpathian region’s geographical position between Ukraine and the EU gives it particular strategic significance as Europe reshapes its energy, logistics and security architecture.
The message emerging from the C8 Summit was clear: economic resilience and security resilience are increasingly inseparable.
Culture as a connector
The C8 initiative was not solely about capital and infrastructure.
The Carpathians share a cultural landscape stretching across national borders - communities, traditions, architecture, food, music and heritage that long pre-date today’s political boundaries.
The summit program included cultural cooperation alongside economic and security discussions, reflecting an understanding that regional integration is ultimately about people more than projects.
In times to come, the cultural dimension could become one of the C8’s greatest strengths, creating a sense of a shared Carpathian identity within a broader European context.
And then there is Bukovel
It was fitting that the summit was held in Bukovel.
The resort has itself become a symbol of economic transformation taking place in Ukraine’s Carpathian region, despite the war.
What was once primarily a mountain destination has developed into a major year-round tourism and investment center, with skiing at its core, augmented by an increasingly diverse hospitality, leisure, property and infrastructure economy.
Bukovel demonstrates what can happen when investment, infrastructure, tourism and entrepreneurial ambition converge. And there is something magical about that convergence in the Carpathians.
Its location also gives the summit a powerful physical metaphor: the same mountains that have historically connected communities are now connecting economies.
A new European crossroad
The long-term significance of the C8 will ultimately be determined not by the declarations made in Bukovel, but by what happens afterwards.
If governments, businesses and private investors can convert the summit’s political framework into functioning transport corridors, energy projects, agricultural value chains, construction programs, tourism networks and cross-border investment, the Carpathians could become one of Europe’s most important emerging economic regions.
For Ukraine, the opportunity is particularly significant.
The Carpathians provide a natural geographical and economic gateway into the EU - and the C8 provides a mechanism for turning that geography into practical cooperation.
For the other seven countries, Ukraine’s reconstruction and economic integration offer access to a vast new market and an unprecedented pipeline of infrastructure, energy, technology and investment opportunities.
And for Europe, the concept is larger still.
The Carpathians could evolve from a mountain range on Europe’s map into a strategic economic bridge between the EU and Ukraine, connecting capital, energy, trade, security and culture across Central and Eastern Europe.
The mountains have always been there. What is new is a shared ambition by neighbors, connected by the mountains, to lift cooperation to loftier heights.

title: 최병광, 하프마라톤 경보 값진 銅…AG 한국 육상 첫 메달
content:
AI 추천 뉴스




최병광, 하프마라톤 경보 값진 銅…AG 한국 육상 첫 메달


한국 경보의 간판 최병광(35)이 2026 아이치·나고야 아시안게임에서 값진 동메달을 목에 걸며 한국 육상에 첫 메달을 안겼다.
최병광은 23일 일본 나고야 도로 코스에서 열린 대회 육상 남자 하프마라톤 경보에서 1시간 28분 35초를 기록해 중국의 스성지(1시간 23분 32초), 일본의 야마니시 도시카즈(1시간 28분 01초)에 이어 세 번째로 결승선을 통과했다. 한국 경보가 아시안게임에서 메달을 따낸 것은 2018년 자카르타·팔렘방 대회 주현명(동메달) 이후 8년 만이다.
레이스 초반 5위를 유지하던 최병광은 12㎞ 지점부터 3위로 올라선 뒤 안정적으로 선두권을 지켰다. 경기 후반 중국과 일본의 주요 경쟁자들이 판정 경고를 받아 주춤하는 사이, 최병광은 흔들림 없는 자세로 페이스를 유지하며 3위 자리를 지켜냈다.
2014년 인천 대회부터 4회 연속 아시안게임에 출전한 최병광은 사실상 생애 마지막 아시안게임이었던 이번 대회에서 첫 메달의 결실을 맺었다. 리우데자네이루, 도쿄, 파리 올림픽을 거치며 한국 경보를 외롭게 이끌어왔지만 이번 대회를 앞두고 메달 후보로 평가받지는 못했다. 그래도 특유의 노련함과 집중력으로 반전을 만들어냈다.
최병광은 경기 후 "어쩌면 마지막이라 생각한 아시안게임에서 메달을 따게 돼 행복하고 기쁘면서도 울컥했다"며 "주변의 부정적인 평가는 신경 쓰지 않고 묵묵히 내 레이스에만 집중했다"고 밝혔다. 이어 "세계무대에 도전할 수 있도록 전폭적으로 지원해 준 소속팀 삼성전자와 대한육상연맹에 감사하다"며 "은퇴하는 날까지 모든 힘을 쏟아내는 선수로 기억되고 싶다. 후배들도 끝까지 도전을 이어가 더 훌륭한 성적을 내주길 바란다"고 덧붙였다.
세계육상연맹은 올해 성인 국제대회 경보 종목 코스를 바꿨다. 기존 20㎞를 21.0975㎞로, 35㎞를 42.195㎞로 바꾸면서 하프마라톤·마라톤 코스와 동일하게 변경했다. 최병광은 거리 조정 후 아시안게임 경보에서 첫 메달을 딴 선수로도 이름을 남기게 됐다.

title: Governo reforça combate à alga invasora com plano nacional até 2030
content:
O Governo aprovou o Programa de Ação Nacional para o Controlo da Macroalga Invasora Rugulopteryx okamurae para o período 2026-2030, com o objetivo de reforçar a prevenção, a deteção precoce e a resposta à expansão da espécie em Portugal.
O plano estabelece uma estratégia integrada para monitorizar, conter e reduzir os impactos da alga, cuja presença se tem vindo a alargar no território nacional. A iniciativa resulta do trabalho de um grupo interinstitucional coordenado pela Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente (APA), que reuniu organismos da Administração Pública, autarquias, instituições científicas e outras entidades.
Originária do Pacífico Norte, a Rugulopteryx okamurae está incluída na lista de espécies exóticas invasoras que suscitam preocupação na União Europeia. Em Portugal continental, os primeiros registos no Sul surgiram em 2021, seguindo-se a expansão pelo Algarve e pela costa alentejana. Em 2024, a espécie foi também identificada ao largo de Cascais. Nos Açores, onde foi detetada pela primeira vez em 2019, já tinha chegado a oito das nove ilhas em 2024.
A elevada capacidade de dispersão e proliferação da alga tem provocado impactos nos ecossistemas marinhos e em atividades económicas ligadas ao litoral. Entre os efeitos apontados estão a diminuição das capturas, danos nas artes de pesca, custos associados à limpeza, perda de atratividade das praias e despesas adicionais para as autarquias com a remoção da biomassa acumulada.
Segundo a Ministra do Ambiente e Energia, Maria da Graça Carvalho, o novo programa pretende substituir intervenções pontuais por uma resposta nacional baseada na ciência, na prevenção e na deteção precoce. A governante reconhece, contudo, que a erradicação da espécie não é, nesta fase, uma possibilidade realista.
Entre as medidas previstas está a criação de uma Base de Dados Nacional Georreferenciada, estações de vigilância em pontos estratégicos, sensores subaquáticos e câmaras remotas em zonas consideradas críticas.
O programa prevê ainda a utilização de imagens de satélite e veículos aéreos não tripulados, além da criação de um sistema de alerta precoce. Serão também desenvolvidos algoritmos capazes de prever a deriva da alga com base nas correntes marítimas e nos ventos.
No terreno, a resposta poderá passar pela remoção manual ou mecânica da alga, pela extração na coluna de água e pela instalação de barreiras de contenção ou deflexão, consoante as características e a sensibilidade de cada local. O transporte e o armazenamento temporário da biomassa recolhida também terão procedimentos específicos.
A investigação científica é outra das áreas contempladas pelo programa. O Governo prevê testar métodos de remoção sustentável, avaliar os impactos ambientais e económicos da espécie e realizar ensaios de restauro ecológico dos ecossistemas depois da remoção.
Está igualmente previsto o estudo de formas de valorização da biomassa recolhida, incluindo a sua caracterização bioquímica e análises de pré-viabilidade para a instalação de unidades de processamento local.
O plano identifica ainda várias potenciais vias de disseminação da espécie, entre as quais as águas de lastro, as incrustações nos cascos das embarcações, os equipamentos de pesca, a aquicultura e a dispersão natural. Para reduzir estes riscos, estão previstas ações de formação, sensibilização e adoção de códigos de boas práticas nos setores envolvidos.
A estratégia inclui também uma componente de comunicação e ciência cidadã, com uma plataforma nacional de informação e registo, sinalização em marinas, portos e zonas de mergulho e materiais informativos para praias e zonas balneares.
O Governo prevê ainda ações dirigidas às comunidades piscatórias, operadores turísticos, aquicultores e praticantes de atividades náuticas, bem como a criação de um canal de comunicação com Espanha e outros países onde a espécie está presente, com o objetivo de reforçar a partilha de informação e a cooperação.

title: Slik vart prestekrisa løyst: – Vi hadde ingen søkarar
content:
Over heile landet står prestestillingar tomme. Den norske kyrkja hadde ved inngangen til året 101,4 tomme stillingar, men no ser fleire prosti lys i tunnelen.
– Vi tullar med å seie at du blir sikra jobb når du er ferdig.
Nytilsett prest i Jølster, Selma Dahle Kraft, kunne fått jobb kor ho ville. Men ho valde å takke ja til jobb i Sunnfjord.
Under heile studieløpet har ho vore klar over at mangelen på prestar er prekær over heile landet.
– Det har vore tema heile vegen. Eg er eigentleg frå Oslo, men eg hadde lyst til å kome meg ut av byen, oppleve naturen.
Lange periodar utan søkarar har tvinga fram mellombelse løysingar og bruk av pensjonistar.
– For eit år sidan gjekk eg ut og sa at vi treng fem nye prestar, og vi hadde ingen søkjarar. Men no har vi fått tilsett i alle dei fem stillingane. Det er vi ganske stolte av, seier prost i Sunnfjord, Knut Magne Nesse.
I dei seks åra han har sete i stillinga, har den uavklarte mannskapssituasjon vore eit gjennomgåande problem.
– Når det blir mellombelse løysingar, blir det ikkje noko langsiktigheit eller målretting i arbeidet. Det går ofte utover arbeidet med konfirmantar, barn og unge. Det er veldig flott at vi har pensjonistar som kan hjelpe oss, men dette var ein situasjon vi måtte ut av.
Satsar på lønn under studiane
Bak den positive snuoperasjonen ligg ein bevisst strategi frå bispedømmet. I Bjørgvin har dei teke i bruk nye og utradisjonelle rekrutteringsmetodar for å trekke til seg folk.
Eitt av dei mest effektive grepa er å tilby studentar som enno ikkje er ferdige med teologistudiet full lønn mot at dei studerer delar av tida.
– Vi har gjort grep i Bjørgvin bispedømme som har gjort at vi har fått mange nye til å søke på prestestillingane, seier biskop Ragnhild Jepsen.
I tillegg har utradisjonelle utdanningsvegar, som erfaringsbasert master, opna dørene for kandidatar med ein annan fagbakgrunn. Jepsen fortel at dei fleste ho har vigsla til prest det siste året, har gått denne vegen.
– Dei får 100 prosent lønn, men dei jobbar 60 prosent og får lov til å studere i 40. Då får ein både praksis samstundes som ein har moglegheit til å følgje studiane. Det ser vi har ein klar effekt, forklarar biskopen.
15 nye prestar det siste året
Resultata av nytenkinga viser seg no over heile bispedømmet. Det siste året er det tilsett 15 nye prestar.
– Ingen kyrkjelag er per i dag heilt utan prest. Vi skaffar prestar til alle gudstenester og kyrkjelege handlingar, seier Jepsen.
Sjølv om bispedømmet framleis er avhengig av pensjonistar i periodar, har tiltaka ført til ei etterlengta fornying i presteskapet.
Heidi Voltersvik Styve har vore kateket i Sunnfjord i 22 år. Tilbodet om løn medan ho studerer var avgjerande for at ho tok steget vidare som prest.
– No kan eg ta det på deltid og jobbe samstundes, og eg har stor glede av det.
I Nidaros bispedøme har mange gjort som Styve i Sunnfjord. Heile 10 prosent av prestestaben har blitt rekrutterte via den nye ordninga.
– Prest under utdanning er ein styrke for kyrkja. Vi hentar folk med ulike erfaringar og bakgrunn, og mange av dei har lokalt tilknyting, seier HR-sjef Håkon Olaussen i Nidaros.
Han strekar under at dei framleis har stillingar som står tomme, men at dei no har 10 nye prestar under utdanning. 6–7 prestar har alt fullført løpet.
Leiar i Kyrkjerådet, Harald Hegstad, meiner erfaringane frå mellom anna Sunnfjord og Nidaros viser at fleire av tiltaka kyrkja har satsa på dei siste åra, verkar.
– Det er eg veldig glad for. Det viser at systematisk og langsiktig arbeid med rekruttering ber frukter. Vi ser det i Sunnfjord, men også andre stader i landet, seier Hegstad.
Han peikar særleg på ordninga med prestar under utdanning og den erfaringsbaserte masterutdanninga, som gjer det mogleg å rekruttere folk som allereie bur i lokalsamfunn som treng prestar.
– På den måten får ein også sterkare lokal forankring, og prestar i lokalsamfunn der det kan vere vanskelegare å få nokon til å flytte til, seier han.
Samstundes meiner Hegstad at tiltaka har hindra at prestemangelen har utvikla seg til ein større krise når store prestekull no går av med pensjon.
Gler seg over unge nyutdanna
Blant dei fem nyutnemnde prestane i Sunnfjord er det også unge, nyutdanna prestar. Det er ikkje kvardagskost i distrikta, der slike kandidatar ofte kan velje og vrake mellom stillingar i heile landet.
– Dei nyutdanna er veldig attraktive. No har vi fått kandidatar som har lyst til å komme til oss. Det er veldig motiverande og gjev ein fantastisk fornying i presteskapet, seier prost Nesse.

title: Yatenga/Kalsaka : 108 acteurs de l’éducation récompensés par la commune
content:
Yatenga/Kalsaka : 108 acteurs de l’éducation récompensés par la commune
Kalsaka, 21 sept. 2026 (AIB)- La commune de Kalsaka a commémoré le samedi 19 septembre les efforts de la communauté éducative en récompensant 108 de l’éducation, a constaté l’AIB sur place.
Cette journée de l’excellence a été placée sous le thème, « L’excellence au service de la Nation : éducation, discipline et patriotisme pour un Burkina Faso meilleur ».
Pour le président de la Délégation spéciale (PDS) de Kalsaka, Antoine Tiendrebéogo, cette initiative va au-delà de la simple reconnaissance des performances scolaires.
« Cette journée entend promouvoir auprès de la jeunesse des valeurs essentielles telles que le travail, la discipline, la responsabilité, le civisme et le patriotisme. Pour nous c’est également un cadre de sensibilisation et d’encouragement des jeunes à persévérer dans leurs études et à s’impliquer davantage dans le développement de la commune et du Burkina Faso »a soutenu le PDS.
Au cours de la cérémonie, des élèves, des enseignants, encadreurs, parents d’élèves et plusieurs autres acteurs du système éducatif ont été récompensés pour leurs efforts consentis pendant l’année scolaire écoulée.
Les récompenses sont composées entre autres d’ordinateurs, de tablettes, de vélos, de kits scolaires et d’attestations de mérite.
Le PDS a exprimé sa reconnaissance au premier responsable de la province pour sa présence, preuve de l’intérêt qu’il porte au secteur de l’éducation et au parrain Adama Sana pour son engagement constant en faveur de l’éducation dans la commune de Kalsaka et pour sa promesse de poursuivre son accompagnement du secteur.
De leur côté, les différents lauréats ont salué la reconnaissance de leurs efforts par les autorités communales et provinciales. Ils ont exprimé leur gratitude et se sont engagés à redoubler d’efforts afin d’améliorer davantage leurs performances au cours de cette année scolaire 2026-2027
La cérémonie a été placée sous la présidence du camarade Haut-commissaire de la province du Yatenga, Pierre Claver Bancé, le parrainage du camarade Adama Sana. Elle s’est déroulée en présence des autorités administratives locales, des représentants des coutumiers, des religieux, de représentants de communes voisines, et de plusieurs acteurs du système éducatif.
